advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Guard the region-prefix strip in _rate_for so it only removes a segment that actually matches a region-code pattern, not any first hyphen segment.
evidence: `body = usage_type[: -len(hit)].rstrip("-")`
`body = body.split("-", 1)[1] if "-" in body else body` — unconditionally drops the first hyphen-delimited segment as a presumed region prefix
Comment claims 'Strip the "USE1-" style region prefix' but nothing verifies the first segment is actually a region code
advisory.finding: _rate_for strips the leading hyphen segment of a usage-type body assuming a region prefix (`body.split("-", 1)[1] if "-" in body else body`), but usage types without a region prefix (or model names whose first hyphen segment is meaningful) will have a real token of the model name discarded, corrupting the normalized comparison key and potentially causing a wrong-model rate match or a miss that falls through to the fail-closed fallback.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide per-region whether a CloudWatch failure should void only that region or the whole metered read, and avoid discarding already-accumulated spend from healthy regions on a single-region error.
evidence: `except ClientError as exc: log.error("CloudWatch metric listing unavailable in %s: %s", region, exc); return None`
`except ClientError as exc: log.error("CloudWatch metric data unavailable in %s: %s", region, exc); return None`
REGIONS default is 'us-east-1,us-west-2' per bedrock_spend_cap.tf, so multi-region is the live config
advisory.finding: _metered_spend sets `found_series` across all regions but returns None on the first region whose list_metrics/get_metric_data raises ClientError, discarding any tokens already accumulated for prior regions. A single unhealthy region thus voids the entire metered signal even when other watched regions returned valid data.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Document/verify intended behavior when a SEED_RATES entry omits 'output', and consider logging when a seed is partially applied.
evidence: `if metric_name == "OutputTokenCount": return prices.get("output")`
bedrock_spend_cap.tf: `output = optional(number)` — output may be absent
When output is absent, seed returns None and _rate_for falls through to input*mult (line 235 uses OutputTokenCount mult) rather than a seeded output rate
advisory.finding: _seed_for returns prices.get("output") for OutputTokenCount with no fallback: a SEED_RATES entry that supplies only 'input' (allowed by the TF variable schema where output is optional()) yields None for output, so _rate_for skips the seed and proceeds to derive output from the input rate — but a seed lacking output silently loses the intended high-erring output seed with no warning.

evidence: bedrock_spend_cap.tf `name = format("bedrock-daily-%s", var.bedrock_daily_cap_usd)`
README.md 'Change the cap: set `bedrock_daily_cap_usd` and apply.'
advisory.finding: The budget resource name embeds the dollar cap: name = format("bedrock-daily-%s", var.bedrock_daily_cap_usd). Because aws_budgets_budget name changes force resource replacement, raising/lowering the cap destroys and recreates the budget (and its notifications) rather than updating in place — contrary to the README's casual 'Change the cap: set bedrock_daily_cap_usd and apply'.

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Preserve 'cached' ce_status (do not force 'unavailable') when a due CE poll fails but a valid same-day cached ce_spend is still held, so the daily release is not blocked by a transient CE error.
evidence: `if state.get("ce_day") == day.isoformat(): ce_spend = float(state.get("ce_spend", float(0))); ce_status = "cached"`
`except ClientError as exc: ce_status = "unavailable"` (line 501) overwrites the 'cached' status while ce_spend keeps the cached value
`if any_attached and spend < THRESHOLD_USD and not signal_unavailable:` (line 559) — release blocked by signal_unavailable
blocking.finding: When a CE poll is 'due' but the API call fails, ce_status is forced back to 'unavailable' (line 501) even though a valid cached ce_spend from earlier today is still held (lines 482-484). This flips signal_unavailable to True and suppresses the automatic daily-release path (line 559 requires `not signal_unavailable`), so a transient CE error can keep the deny attached even when both a cached CE number and the metered signal agree spend is under the cap.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Derive the Logs/SSM ARN region from var.aws_region (or a shared local) instead of the hardcoded "us-east-1" so IAM scoping tracks the actual deployment region.
evidence: provider "aws" { region = var.aws_region } (infra/terraform/main.tf:5-7)
variable "aws_region" { ... default = "us-east-1" } (infra/terraform/variables.tf:1-5)
Logs ARN: format("arn:aws:logs:%s:%s:log-group:/aws/lambda/%s:*", "us-east-1", ...)
State ARN: format("arn:aws:ssm:%s:%s:parameter/%s/state", "us-east-1", ...) (bedrock_spend_cap.tf:317-320)
aws_cloudwatch_log_group.bedrock_spend_cap has no explicit region and inherits the provider (var.aws_region)
dropped.finding: The Lambda execution-role IAM policy hardcodes the region literal "us-east-1" in its Logs and State (SSM) ARN scoping, but the aws_cloudwatch_log_group and the SSM state parameter are created in the provider region (var.aws_region). If var.aws_region is ever set to anything other than us-east-1, the least-privilege grants no longer match the resources' region and the Lambda loses logs:PutLogEvents / ssm:GetParameter+PutParameter, silently disabling enforcement.
scenarios: Operator overrides var.aws_region to a non-us-east-1 value; Lambda cannot write logs or read/write its state parameter and enforcement quietly stops.
dropped.suggested_fix: Replace the literal "us-east-1" in the Logs and State statements with var.aws_region (or a local bedrock_cap_region shared with the log group and SSM parameter).

dropped.finding: The deny policy is attached/detached to the Admin IAM group (default target), giving this Lambda a large blast radius over human admin credentials; a bug or mis-set threshold denies Bedrock to every admin at once.
scenarios: A lowered bedrock_daily_cap_usd or a metering/pricing error trips the cap and attaches the deny to the Admin group, blocking all admins' Bedrock access simultaneously.
